chapter: Chicago memories and the road to the Navy
title: Ethel Waters and the four-in-a-bar Charleston; Tim Moore
summary: Zutty says Ethel Waters taught him the Charleston singing James P. Johnson's tune; he could not manage two in a bar, so played four in a bar. Tim Moore's boxing act with a midget is recalled.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Did you say that it was Ethel Walters that taught you the Charleston?

Yes indeed. She sure did. Because she was singing that James P. Johnson, 'Charleston, Charleston.' You know she'd get right, I was down in the pit, but she was up on the stage and she would (SOUND OF CLAPPING). But I couldn't make it with two in a bar. So when I put that four in a bar that made that Charleston. I could make it with that. Yes. And Tim Moore, he was on circuit then. Him and a midget used to have a prize fight. They had a little scene in there where he and this midget would fight like. And this midget beat Tim Moore so he made Tim Moore ring the bell.
Yes, that's that Southern accent now.
